conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes 'Yes' to the claim, stating that evidence supports regular consumption of cranberry juice or extract in reducing the frequency of recurrent cystitis and UTIs in women.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion:** **Yes.** Evidence supports that regular consumption of cranberry juice or cranberry extract can reduce the frequency of recurrent cystitis and lower-level urinary tract infections (UTIs) in women.

**Evidence Summary:**
* **Risk Reduction:** A comprehensive 2023 Cochrane systematic review analyzing 50 randomized clinical trials found that cranberry products significantly reduce the risk of repeat, symptomatic, culture-confirmed UTIs in women prone to recurrence by roughly 26% (https://medicalxpress.com/news/2023-04-cranberry-juice-recurrent-utis-people.html, https://cobfoundation.org/health-information/cranberry-vs-d-mannose-for-uti-prevention/). Additional systematic reviews report similar risk reductions of approximately 30% to 32% (https://www.gleneagles.com.sg/health-plus/article/cranberry-juice-recurrent-utis-women).
* **Biological Mechanism:** Cranberries contain bioactive compounds known as proanthocyanidins (PACs). PACs inhibit uropathogenic bacteria—primarily *Escherichia coli*—from adhering to the mucosal lining of the bladder and urinary tract, allowing bacteria to be flushed out during urination (https://www.21stcentury.com.my/wellness-resource/cranberry-juice-and-urinary-tract-infection-uti/).
* **Clinical Significance:** While the overall magnitude of risk reduction is modest and results may vary depending on dosage, PAC concentration, and individual compliance, regular intake of either cranberry juice or daily cranberry extract supplements serves as an effective non-antibiotic preventive measure (https://cobfoundation.org/health-information/cranberry-vs-d-mannose-for-uti-prevention/, https://medicalxpress.com/news/2023-04-cranberry-juice-recurrent-utis-people.html).
